newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on retail buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on retail buying.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied to finish with modest gains after retail speculators moved in ahead of monthly economic data due on Thursday, traders said on Tuesday.
The SET Index closed rising 6.93 points to 826.72 on sluggish, holiday-thinned three billion baht turnover. The SET 50 ended gaining 0.49 point at 61.69.
"The market is up a bit thanks to retail investors although most our clients are already away for Christmas," said a trader at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The Bank of Thailand is due to release on Thursday new monthly economic data, including October current account and trade deficits, which local investors expect may prove more positive than those in recent months.
Brokers said the absence of foreign players slowed sales of banks and other blue chip stocks which had been targets of market sell-off in the past week.
"There are still plenty of sell orders from foreign houses out there but people are on holiday, giving a chance for retail buying to outweigh foreign sales," said an analyst at a European broker.
Finance and bank stocks headed the active list. Bangkok Bank ended down one baht at 193, Thai Farmers Bank rose two to 127, and Finance One added 0.50 to 52.
